subject: Genetics
title: Typos in the Code
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Typos in the Code.

hook.text: Your cells copy 3 billion DNA letters every time they divide. Mistakes happen—about 1 per 100 million bases.

buildup.text: Most typos are harmless. The genetic code has redundancy built in—multiple codons produce the same amino acid.

discovery.text: But sometimes a single letter change hits a critical spot. Sickle cell anemia is one letter—A to T—in one gene.

twist.text: That same sickle cell mutation protects against malaria. A typo can be a curse and a shield at once.

climax.text: Mutations aren't good or bad by nature. Context decides. Environment is the judge; DNA is the defendant.

punchline.text: A typo in your DNA could save your life.

quiz.question: What determines whether a mutation is harmful or beneficial?
